A1.justification: Both complete 36-page PDFs describe the same work. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable comparison of all figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A-D. Differences are confined to the version stamp and acknowledgment.

before.justification: v1 reports original module evaluations, a physical tactile-graphics study with 15 participants, and additional swell-paper comparisons (Tables 1-2, A4-A5).

after.justification: v2 retains these original quantitative evaluations and participant studies, including their numerical results and qualitative findings.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain the same geometry generation, texture synthesis and tiling, displacement, base flattening, braille placement, and interactive procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same real/synthetic texture data, tactile sensor library, object and texture evaluations, participant populations, and swell-paper comparison scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices B and D, including Qwen, Nano Banana Pro, Tiled Diffusion, Hunyuan3D 2.1, Trellis 2, Naive, TactileNet, expert-designed swell-paper graphics, MatFuse, and TexGaussian.

E3.justification: The 50-prompt geometry/texture evaluations, 15-participant study using 48 artifacts, and appendix study protocols are identical. Training settings, inference configurations, metrics, preprocessing, and controls are unchanged.

E4.justification: The base-plate and tiling ablations, baseline failure cases, and extended participant-feedback analyses are retained unchanged (Figures 4-5 and A2-A4; Appendix C).

E5.justification: The uncertainty reporting in Tables 2, A4, and A5 and the paired t-tests over 240 observations in Section 4.3 are identical. No run-count, seed, or statistical-estimation information is added.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative findings match across the main text and appendices. For example, Table 2 retains Ours ratings of 3.93 ± 1.32 for BLV participants and 3.35 ± 1.39 for blindfolded sighted participants.

T1.justification: The filtering, displacement, and flattening equations in Section 3, topology-preservation reasoning in Appendix A.5, and metric definitions in Appendix B are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same integrated text-to-tactile-graphics contribution and claims about fabrication readiness, tactile detail, braille integration, and user preference.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same interpretations of braille, relief amplitude, directionality, and texture cues, together with the touch-only recognition limitation and small, locally recruited participant-sample caveat.

D1.justification: Implementation details, prompts, hyperparameters, hardware, training time, fabrication specifications, and project/code access information are unchanged. The added NVIDIA Academic Grant acknowledgment supplies funding credit, not new technical or resource-access information.

R1.justification: Section 2, the 75-reference bibliography, and positioning relative to earlier tactile-graphics and generative methods are identical.

P1.justification: Page 15 adds an NVIDIA Academic Grant to the funding acknowledgment, with a small accompanying wording adjustment. The first-page arXiv version/date stamp is updated. Research prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The longer acknowledgment causes localized line wrapping and spacing adjustments on page 15, and the first-page version stamp changes. All figures, tables, and appendix layouts are identical.

improvement.justification: v2 adds a funding credit and updates the version stamp, with minor acknowledgment reflow. Although acknowledgment completeness improves slightly, the methods, evidence, reasoning, limitations, and reproducibility information remain identical throughout both PDFs. These administrative edits do not meaningfully change overall paper quality.
